observation.visible_scene: A sunny outdoor playground with artificial green turf, maroon support posts, and a play structure with a cream slide in the background under a blue sky. A young child in a dark long-sleeve shirt, olive pants and sneakers sits in a teal bucket-style swing seat, gripping the two metal chains with both hands. Long shadows of the posts and swing chains stretch across the turf. The camera is fixed: the left and right posts and the background play structure hold constant positions in the frame throughout.
visible_changes: The child and swing seat move along a pendulum-like arc: the chains tilt toward the right side of the frame (frames 1-6), then swing toward vertical and lean left (frames 7-15), then return toward the right (frames 16-30), then lean left again (frames 31-41), indicating continuous back-and-forth swinging already in progress at the first frame and still ongoing at the last.

The child's body posture cycles between a reclined position with legs lifted and extended forward (frames 1-6) and a more upright/forward-leaning position with legs dangling and feet lower (frames 7-15, 31-41), with the legs tucking and re-extending as the swing changes direction.
The child's face, partly hidden behind the raised arm in the early frames, becomes visible facing the camera in the middle and later frames (e.g. frames 7-15, 31-41).
The empty second swing seat to the right remains stationary, hanging from its chains, while only the child's swing moves.
The child's horizontal position within the frame shifts only modestly, consistent with the swing arc being largely toward and away from the camera rather than side-to-side.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the swinging was initiated (an earlier push or self-pumping before the crop) and whether the motion continues, slows, or stops after the last frame are not shown.
Whether the leg extension/tucking is deliberate pumping to maintain amplitude or incidental body motion cannot be determined from the clip alone.
uncertain_details: The exact number of completed swing cycles within the excerpt is hard to count due to the toward/away arc and limited sampling.
Minor apparent size changes of the child could be depth along the swing arc rather than any zoom; camera zoom is not clearly evidenced.
The precise timing of direction reversals between sampled frames is interpolated, not directly observed.
